[P2] 出版者的话
古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：“任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地，对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。
现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。
情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期，一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心发展影响很长远。
当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露，就能生根、发芽。
这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。
让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧！

[P3] 老师对你说
把阳光收藏在心里
一看到故事的名字，就被这个“惊喜礼物”所吸引，迫不及待地想看看到底是什么礼物。小河狸为什么会收到礼物呢？原来是河狸家族要给所有去年出生的河狸宝宝们庆祝生日。河狸爸爸和妈妈们真有创意，他们组织了一场盛大的联欢活动，还把礼物都藏到了森林里。河狸宝宝们好期待啊！都想在夺宝游戏中找到自己心仪的礼物。
不过，小河狸找到的却是一件普通得不能再普通的礼物，至少一开始他是这样认为的。他看到别人找到礼物时都很开心，觉得别人的礼物都比自己的好，尤其是哥哥波吕克斯的礼物，更是让小河狸羡慕得不得了。小河狸想借哥哥的礼物玩，可是哥哥没有答应。
平静下来的小河狸仔细地欣赏自己的礼物，他觉得这份礼物一定有它的用途。你一定猜不到，这份礼物竟然给了小河狸一个又一个惊喜，连哥哥都主动想要和他交换礼物玩呢！到底是什么礼物呢？让我们一起来读故事吧！
其实，在生活中，我们会或多或少地从小河狸身上看到自己的影子，也会遇到一些令自己不满意的事情：没有买到自己喜欢的玩具；做游戏时没能和好朋友分在一个小组；爸爸妈妈没有时间陪我们玩……

[P4] 遇到这些事情时，我们是否可以像小河狸那样换一个角度思考问题呢？我们是否能像小河狸那样学会珍惜自己所拥有的呢？我们可能没有别人的玩具汽车，但是我们可以用积木搭房子、搭汽车；假如好朋友没在身边，那就和身边的朋友好好玩，一样很快乐；若爸爸妈妈没有时间陪我们，我们可以自己画画、看书。
这样想了，这样做了，结果就会大不同。所以说，快乐与否全凭我们自己决定，并不取决于我们得到了多少或拥有了多少。你想让自己快乐，就多想些让自己高兴的事情，多做些自己喜欢的事情。学会接受我们所得到的和拥有的，用心体会，就会发现世界的美好，就会发现快乐其实一直在我们身边。
（保定市教科所教研员 刘育红）

[P5] 今天可真是个大日子！
河狸家族要给所有去年出生的河狸宝宝们庆祝生日！
趁着这个机会，河狸爸爸和妈妈们组织了一场盛大的联欢活动。
他们还把礼物都藏到了森林里，一场真正的寻宝游戏开始啦！

[P8] 小河狸跑向一根树枝，树枝上面挂着一只袜子。
小河狸觉得那只袜子里面和他的礼物。
他把爪子伸进里面摸了摸：什么都没有！
他有点急躁，把脑袋伸进了袜子里，上半身也钻了进去，结果，一不小心，他就掉到那只袜子里头了。
他从里面掏出了一片涂有清漆的树叶。树叶大大的，有着精致的叶脉和锯齿状的叶缘——一个来自大自然的小礼物！
不过，小河狸觉得有一点点失望。

一个全新的弹弓！
他十分高兴，在橡皮筋上放上一颗石子，瞄准了挂在树上的一颗松果。

他用手指比划着，假装自己在拿着弹弓玩：瞄准，发射，

[P16] “你可以把弹弓借给我玩一玩吗？”小河狸满怀希望地问哥哥。
可是，他的哥哥用力地摇着头。
“想都别想！你太小了，会弄伤自己的！”哥哥毫不客气地答道，摆起了大人的架子。
小河狸是河狸宝宝中最晚出生的，算起来的确比其他宝宝要小。
但是，他的年龄却和大家一样呀！
“这太不公平了！”小河狸生气地想。

[P18] 小河狸赌气走开了。
他登上爸爸妈妈的水坝，在一根高高的、单独伸出来的树枝上坐了下来。
就像安慰小河狸似的，一阵风吹来，把树枝吹得像秋千一样轻轻地晃动。

[P20] 小河狸平静下来。
他仔细地盯着树叶：它看起来比之前更闪亮了。
“嘿！”他对着树叶做了个鬼脸！
“为什么要送给我一片树叶呢？”小河狸琢磨着，
想搞清楚这是怎么回事。
“这片树叶一定有它的用处……”

[P21] 小河狸把树叶在面前展开：是不是可以做一张桌布？
把它折叠起来的话，还可以当成是收纳玩具用的小包。
小河狸不太确定：“哼！这样就太没意思啦！”，

他把树叶放在头上，像系头巾一样，把树叶的两端系在一起。
“我这样是不是很可爱呢？”，

[P24] 就在这时，一滴雨从树叶上滚下来，溅到了小河狸的脚指头上。
小河狸乐了：“一片不渗水的树叶！”
他小心地把树叶展开，然后像撑伞一样把它举在头顶。

[P25] 突然，一阵狂风吹来，吹动了小河狸坐着的那根树枝。
小河狸还没站稳，就失去了平衡，掉了下去。
“救命啊！”他一边大喊，一边紧紧地抓住树叶。

[P28] 大风把树叶吹得鼓鼓的。
树叶随风飘舞，在空中划了几道弧后，慢慢降落在水面上。
小河狸像一片羽毛一样着陆了。
“哇！太棒了！”小河狸的哥哥惊叹道，并朝小河狸跑去，“可以把你的树叶借给我玩一下吗？我把我的弹弓给你，如果你想要的话……”
小河狸微笑着答道：“我们还是一起玩吧！”

[P29] 兄弟俩爬上水坝，轮流玩耍着。
小河狸很轻，总是可以在空中翻出漂亮的跟头。
哥哥羡慕地望着他。
“你是怎么做到的呢？”哥哥嫉妒地问道。
“你个头太大了，而且对于我的树叶来说也太重了！”
小河狸解释道，眼里有一丝狡黠。

[P31] 小河狸对着哥哥哈哈大笑起来：
“你把弹弓给我，我想到一个好主意啦！
小河狸拿弹弓瞄准枫树顶端最大的几片叶子……
“快过来帮我呀！”他一边捡着地上的叶子和松针，一边对哥哥说。
小河狸教哥哥用这些枫叶做一只大风筝。

[P33] 他们做的风筝好大呀，兄弟俩终于可以一起在空中飞翔啦！
他们发明了新的玩法，还在空中划出了好多弧。
“两个人一起玩才更有意思，你不觉得吗？”哥哥笑着说。
小河狸十分开心，这才是他最好的生日礼物呢！

[P2] Publisher's Note
The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry, and that's not difficult. But to be angry at the right time, in the right place, with the right person, and in the right way, that's difficult.' What we now call emotional management means expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time and place, and toward the right person.
In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills, because those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this skill, though perhaps intelligent, often struggle in their endeavors.
While emotional management skills are partly influenced by innate factors, they ultimately depend on learning and cultivation. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this period create lasting neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.
Currently, the practice of parent-child reading of emotional management picture books is widely recognized as an effective way to cultivate these skills. Quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried by parents' voices into children's ears, taking root in their hearts, and with sunlight and rain, they can grow and sprout.
This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks focuses on specific emotional topics for children, illustrating their inner journeys and revealing how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a reference for parents during shared reading.
Let us enjoy a wonderful parent-child reading journey with this series!

[P3] Teacher Says to You
Keep the Sunshine in Your Heart
As soon as you see the title of the story, you're drawn to this 'surprise gift' and can't wait to find out what it is. Why would the little beaver receive a gift? It turns out the beaver family is celebrating the birthdays of all the beaver babies born last year. The beaver dads and moms are so creative—they organized a grand party and hid all the gifts in the forest. The baby beavers are so excited! They all want to find their favorite gift in the treasure hunt game.
However, the gift the little beaver finds is ordinary—so ordinary that at first, he thinks it's nothing special. He sees others find their gifts and feel happy, and he thinks everyone else's gift is better than his, especially his brother Polux's gift, which makes the little beaver envious. The little beaver wants to borrow his brother's gift to play with, but his brother doesn't agree.
Calm down, the little beaver carefully examines his gift and feels it must have a purpose. You won't guess this—the gift actually brings one surprise after another to the little beaver, and even his brother wants to trade gifts with him! What could the gift be? Let's read the story together!
In real life, we can often see parts of ourselves in the little beaver, and we also face things that make us unhappy: not getting the toy we want; not being able to be in the same group as our best friend during games; parents not having time to play with us...
Welcome to follow Songta Beibe, free to share
The growth treasure trove of playful and explorative Songta Beibe

[P4] When we encounter these situations, can we think about problems from a different angle, just like little beaver? Can we learn to cherish what we have, just like little beaver? We might not have others' toy cars, but we can build houses and cars with building blocks; if our good friends are not around, we can play happily with friends nearby; if our parents don't have time to accompany us, we can draw or read books by ourselves.
Thinking this way and acting this way will lead to very different results. Therefore, whether we are happy depends entirely on ourselves, not on how much we have received or own. If you want to be happy, think more about things that make you happy, and do more things you enjoy. Learn to accept what we have received and own, appreciate it with our hearts, and we will discover the beauty of the world, and realize that happiness is always right by our side.
(Researcher, Baoding City Education Research Institute, Liu Yuhong)

[P5] Today is truly a big day!
The beaver family is celebrating the birthdays of all the beaver babies born last year!
Taking this opportunity, the beaver dads and moms have organized a grand celebration.
They've even hidden the gifts in the forest—let the real treasure hunt begin!

[P8] The little beaver ran toward a branch, where a sock was hanging.
The little beaver thought his gift was inside that sock.
He put his paw in and felt around: nothing!
He got a bit impatient, stuck his head into the sock, and then his upper body too. As a result, he accidentally fell right into the sock.
He pulled out a leaf coated with clear varnish. The leaf was big, with delicate veins and serrated edges — a little gift from nature!
However, the little beaver felt a little bit disappointed.

[P9] He saw his brothers and sisters showing off their gifts:
Nest received a bag of hazelnuts, and Romani received a necklace made of sunflower seeds.
They all smiled with satisfaction.

[P11] Across from the little beaver, his brother Polux also opened his gift and took out
a brand new slingshot!
He was very happy, placed a stone on the rubber band, and aimed at a pinecone hanging on the tree.
The pinecone fell to the ground beneath the tree, ready to eat!

[P14] "A slingshot, this is amazing!" the little beaver thought enviously.
He pretended to hold a slingshot with his fingers, aiming, shooting,
knocking down pinecones, stealing victory's fruit from predators.
His brother is so lucky!

[P16] "Can you lend me your slingshot to play with for a bit?" the little beaver asked his brother full of hope.
But his brother shook his head firmly.
"Don't even think about it! You're too small, you might hurt yourself!" the brother replied without hesitation, putting on an adult's air.
The little beaver was the last-born among the beaver babies, and indeed, he was smaller than the others.
But his age was the same as everyone else's!
"This is so unfair!" the little beaver thought angrily.

[P18] The little beaver stormed off.
He climbed onto his parents' dam and sat on a tall, solitary branch that stuck out.
As if comforting the little beaver, a breeze blew, making the branch sway gently like a swing.

[P20] The little beaver calmed down.
He stared carefully at the leaf: it looked brighter than before.
"Hey!" He made a funny face at the leaf!
"Why send me a leaf?" the little beaver pondered,
trying to figure out what was going on.
"This leaf must have its use..."

[P21] The little beaver spread the leaf out in front of him: Could it be used as a tablecloth?
If he folded it up, it could also be a small bag for storing toys.
The little beaver wasn't sure: "Hmph! That's just too boring!"

He put the leaf on his head, tying the two ends together like a headscarf.
"Am I cute like this?"

[P24] Just then, a drop of rain rolled off a leaf and splashed onto the little beaver's toe.
The little beaver smiled: "A leaf that doesn't let water through!"
He carefully unfolded the leaf and held it over his head like an umbrella.

[P25] Suddenly, a strong wind blew, shaking the branch where the little beaver was sitting.
The little beaver hadn't stood steady yet and lost his balance, falling down.
"Help!" he shouted, while tightly grabbing the leaf.

[P28] The strong wind blew the leaf鼓鼓的.
The leaf danced in the wind, drew a few arcs in the air, and slowly landed on the water surface.
The little beaver landed like a feather.
"Wow! Amazing!" exclaimed the little beaver's brother, running towards him, "Can I borrow your leaf to play with for a while? I'll give you my slingshot if you want it..."
The little beaver smiled and replied, "Let's play together!"

[P29] The two brothers climbed onto the dam and took turns playing.
The little beaver was light, and could always flip a beautiful somersault in the air.
His brother looked at him enviously.
"How did you do that?" the brother asked, jealous.
"You're too big, and too heavy for my leaf!" the little beaver explained, with a hint of mischief in his eyes.

[P31] The little beaver laughed happily at his brother:
"Give me the slingshot, I've got a great idea!"
The little beaver aimed the slingshot at the largest leaves at the top of the maple tree...
"Come and help me!" he said, picking up leaves and pine needles from the ground while talking to his brother.
The little beaver taught his brother to make a big kite out of these maple leaves.

[P33] The kite they made was so big! The two brothers could finally fly together in the sky!
They invented a new way to play and drew many arcs in the air.
"Playing together is more fun, don't you think?" the older brother said with a smile.
The little beaver was very happy. This was the best birthday gift ever!
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《小河狸的惊喜礼物》的封面，展示了书名、作者、译者、出版社信息以及一只头顶绿叶、穿着条纹上衣和绿色短裤的小河狸插图。
[P2] 本页为绘本《小河狸的惊喜礼物》的出版者序言，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的关键期，并介绍了该系列图画书通过亲子共读帮助孩子认识和管理情绪的教育理念。
[P3] 本页为绘本《小河狸的惊喜礼物》的导读页，通过‘老师对你说’栏目，介绍了故事背景：河狸家族为去年出生的宝宝们举办生日寻宝活动，小河狸起初因收到普通礼物而羡慕他人，但最终发现礼物的惊喜。同时，页面引导读者思考生活中类似的情绪体验，并鼓励亲子共读。
[P4] 本页为绘本的导读或教育建议部分，通过小河狸的例子，引导孩子学会换角度思考、珍惜已有事物，并强调快乐源于内心感受而非物质拥有，最后署名为保定市教科所教研员刘育红。
